name: 15h lora forward pass
title: A LoRA layer adds a thin trainable path beside a frozen matrix
subtitle: Toy layer with width 3 and rank r = 1; scale alpha / r set to 1; same numbers as the note

steps.caption: LoRA keeps the pretrained matrix W frozen (gray) and adds a path through two thin matrices. Training starts with B = 0, so the new path adds nothing and the model begins exactly where it was.
The frozen path is the ordinary layer. Row 1 of W times x: 2×2 + 0×4 + 1×6 = 10.
The frozen path is the ordinary layer. Row 2 of W times x: 0×2 + 1×4 + 0×6 = 4.
The frozen path is the ordinary layer. Row 3 of W times x: 1×2 + 0×4 + 1×6 = 8.
After training, A = (0.5, 0.5, 0) and B = (1, 0, 2). A squeezes the 3 inputs into r = 1 number: A x = 3. A rank of 1 means every update this adapter makes points along one direction.
B spreads that one number back out to 3 outputs: B × 3 = (3, 0, 6).
The layer output adds the two paths: h = W x + B A x = (13, 4, 14). Gradients only change A and B, so W stays exactly as pretrained.
Merging for serving: add BA into W once. Row 1 of the merged matrix times x gives 13, the same as before, with no extra work per token.
Merging for serving: add BA into W once. Row 2 of the merged matrix times x gives 4, the same as before, with no extra work per token.
Merging for serving: add BA into W once. Row 3 of the merged matrix times x gives 14, the same as before, with no extra work per token.
The toy adapter trains 6 numbers instead of 9. On the story model a rank 16 adapter on one 384 × 384 query projection trains 2 × 384 × 16 = 12,288 numbers instead of 147,456.
